entities.summary: Sextus Quinctilius was a Roman consul of the Quinctilia gens, born into a prominent family in ancient Rome. As a consul, Sextus Quinctilius played a significant role in the governance of Rome, contributing to the Republic's stability and growth. He served as consul from 453 BCE until his death in 452 BCE, succumbing to a pestilence that ravaged the city. This event highlights the vulnerability of even the most powerful cities to disease. The Roman Republic's governance structure and the Quinctilia gens' influence on Roman politics remain important topics for historians and scholars today.
